The four nonzero-salt S1/S6 predictions below pass the fixed numerical
solution checks. S1's aqueous emim-cation-equivalent mass fraction and S6's
organic TBP mole fraction are different observables. Their differences from
measurements and paper-model values are descriptive. A compact table keeps
these few scalar comparisons and their distinct units visible; a continuous
curve is not established by these rows.

```{python}
import json, pandas as pd
from pathlib import Path
records = json.loads(Path('results/subsystem-comparison.json').read_text())
declaration = json.loads(Path('inputs/lithium-declarations.json').read_text())
comparison = pd.json_normalize(records)
display(comparison.filter(regex='^(table|quantity|source\\.|candidate|admitted|minus_|absolute_)'))
display(comparison.groupby('table')[['absolute_measured_error','absolute_published_error']].mean())
display(pd.json_normalize(records,record_path='phases',meta='table'))
display(pd.DataFrame(records).filter(regex='balance|chemical|phase_distance|numerical_limits|convergence'))
display(pd.Series(declaration['assumptions'],name="Lithium's benchmark assumptions"))
```

Hubach et al., DOI 10.1021/acs.jced.4c00074, Tables 2–4 and SI S1/S6
supply the tuples and comparison columns. Exact source hashes and locators
are in `inputs/source/source_manifest.json`; Lithium's read-only paths,
commit and hashes are in `inputs/lithium-declarations.json`.

Lithium's benchmark assumptions are the neutral ionic-liquid pseudo-component,
equal aqueous-solution and solvent masses, pressure, association edges and
diameter choices shown above. Native C++ evaluates the water correlations,
association edges, feed conversion, equilibrium and projections. Both liquids
support all subsystem species and impose electroneutrality with electrochemical
equilibrium. Fixed starting compositions, independent of source targets, are
recorded in the producer. The aqueous phase is identified by greater water
mass fraction. The displayed numerical limits are, in order, composition
normalization, component balance in mol, phase charge in mol per mol, relative
pressure and chemical/electrochemical residual in units of RT. These limits
are separate from measurement uncertainty.

Lithium's benchmark assumption retains the Engine dispersion rule
$u_{ij}=\sqrt{u_i u_j}(1-k_{ij})$ with printed coefficients unchanged.
Hubach Eq. (6) prints $u_{ij}=\sqrt{u_i u_j(1-k_{ij})}$, visually checked
in PDF CBJZ36VC p. 3 (full locator in `inputs/lithium-declarations.json`). No coefficient remapping is made.
This rule difference, the benchmark/source pressures displayed above and
unknown source feed ratio preclude exact source parity. Their separate
effects are not identified by this comparison; remaining discrepancy causes
are undetermined.

The SI expanded uncertainties are 0.0162 for S1 and 0.039 for S6, with
coverage factor 2; standard temperature uncertainty is 0.5 K. These source
scales do not quantify uncertainty in Lithium's benchmark assumptions.
Paper-model columns are rounded to four decimal places. No physical
pass threshold or independent physical validation follows from these fitted
data comparisons. Zero-salt rows, S11 extraction, charged emim/tcb exchange
and global stability remain excluded. Independent delivered review is pending;
this notebook has not been promoted for manuscript use.
